meta.title: HeroGame Art Studio
launch.title: Open Art Studio from the local service
launch.body: You opened the page source file. Art Studio needs the local service to read projects, save work, and connect to AI.
launch.step1: In the project root, double-click start.command (macOS) and wait for the browser to open.
launch.step2: Keep the launch terminal open while working; press Ctrl+C to stop.
launch.note: Use the button above when the service is already running. For first-time setup, follow the project README; on Windows / Linux, in an activated venv run python launch.py (from the studio directory).
lineGate.lead: Pick a product line first. Fighting-game and desk-pet portraits use different projects and must not be mixed.
lineGate.herogame.title: Fighting-game assets
lineGate.herogame.desc: Style lock · stages · hero sheets · commit to battle
lineGate.deskpet.title: Desk-pet / portrait assets
lineGate.deskpet.desc: Style lock · action list · de-cyan export transparent frames
lineGate.hint: API Key / provider / models are remembered per product line. Project folders and asset dirs are fully isolated.
projectGate.title: Choose a project
projectGate.lead: Create an empty folder, or open an existing project for this product line.
projectGate.aliasPlaceholder: Leave blank to use the folder name
menubar.brandSub: Pick a product line to enter the workspace
menubar.inboxEmpty: No tasks yet. Generate art or open a project and they will show up here.
project.foldHint: Projects for the current product line. Switching never jumps to the other line.
api.keyPlaceholder: Paste a Key starting with AQ. or AI…
api.keyStatusUnset: No API Key set for this product line yet.
api.hintSession: By default the key stays in this service session only; check the box to store it in the system credential store. Keys are never written to the project or browser storage. Each product line has its own settings; they apply to the next task.
api.hintPrefix: Prefixes are only a hint—the real source is the page where you created the Key. Choose manually if detection is wrong. The connection check uses countTokens only; it does not generate images or voice and cannot prove every capability works.
style.title: Style lock
style.lead: Each project has one style lock. Write the prompt → draft → commit to lock it; it cannot be changed afterward. Then make stages, heroes, or portraits.
style.notesPlaceholder: Optional. e.g. harder outlines, silhouette closer to Bleach vs Naruto, no chibi.
style.upload: Or upload an existing style image
style.promptPlaceholder: After you click “① Write image prompt”, the English prompt appears here.
style.frozen: This project’s style is locked and cannot be changed or undone.
stages.title: Stage brief
stages.lead: When a stage is open, “Write prompt” updates that stage and does not create a new entry. For a brand-new place, click “New stage” first. Standable floors and platforms must share one side-view layer (step cross-section)—do not use 3/4 perspective that pushes platforms into the background.
stages.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Qin terracotta army pits, deep ochre ranks, distant tomb gate and cold moon.
stages.keywordsPlaceholder: tomb, clay, cold moon, standable ground
stages.refNone: No reference (leave empty for the first one)
stages.exportPackTitle: Zip this project’s committed stage and send it to the battle client to import.
stages.bgmHint: Lyria 3 Clip · needs an AI Studio Key and model access; Express does not offer this API yet. 30s instrumental loop with fighting pressure (less cheerful melody). Reads visual plus optional stage art; on commit writes bgm into stage.json for the battle client to loop.
stages.deleteHint: Delete clears studio settings, drafts, and committed assets/game/stages/. The next battle on the play client will no longer show this stage.
portraits.title: Portrait brief
portraits.lead: Separate from battle heroes: cyan-screen action strips → split → de-cyan export transparent PNG locally. No fighter files, nothing under game/heroes.
portraits.appearancePlaceholder: e.g. little fox desk pet with a red scarf, round ears and fluffy tail, readable side silhouette.
portraits.gearPlaceholder: e.g. red scarf, small bell, cloth pouch.
portraits.planHint: Set categories and frame counts, then write prompts
portraits.planLead: Check actions to generate; change frame counts (turnaround fixed at 4). You can add custom categories. Inference only writes prompts for the list—it will not invent slots.
portraits.genAllTitle: Needs a turnaround draft first; only generates actions that are still missing
portraits.revealTitle: Open this portrait’s export folder in Finder / File Explorer
portraits.unifyBodyTitle: Scale all action draft strips to the reference action torso height (idle or walk, etc.) with NEAREST. Does not regenerate art.
portraits.bodyScaleTitle: Compare each sheet to the guide, tweak, write back drafts and auto de-cyan export. Needs at least one action-strip draft.
portraits.help: Edit prompts on cards anytime—they autosave. Or click “Refine prompt” to describe what you dislike and rewrite, then “Generate draft / Try another”. Action strips must match the turnaround character; no cyan/teal on the body (for de-cyan cutout). Discard a draft to regenerate. Saving in body-scale writes the draft and auto de-cyan exports that slot’s transparent frames. “Delete this portrait” clears settings, drafts, and exported frames.
heroes.title: Hero brief
heroes.appearancePlaceholder: e.g. young Nurhaci, fur hat, wild-boar leather armor, solid build, readable side silhouette as a banner commander.
heroes.refHint: If likeness is off, upload a front / half-body photo. Generating the turnaround aligns face and body into a pixel character; outfit still follows the text. Later action strips follow the turnaround—no need to reattach the photo per slot.
heroes.gearPlaceholder: e.g. waist saber, horn bow, banner flag, armor plates and fur trim.
heroes.kitPlaceholder: e.g. grounded normals slash; up+normal rising; down+normal aerial slam; special forward cast; up+special anti-air; down+special air-to-ground; super summons cavalry.
heroes.lead: Fill only these three. The system infers keyframe prompts (actions + projectile fx_*) and moves numbers. Generate and commit the turnaround alone first, then one-click the rest (3 at a time). After art, split and preview before commit; splitting does not write to the game. Source art is kept so you can re-split without regenerating. Generation runs in the background—switch to another hero or stage while you wait.
heroes.unifyBodyTitle: Scale committed action strips to idle torso height (ignoring weapons/particle spikes) with NEAREST. Does not regenerate art.
heroes.bodyScaleTitle: In-page workspace: compare each sheet to the guide, tweak per-frame size, and commit directly.
heroes.exportPackTitle: Zip this project’s committed hero and send it to the battle client. Does not write into someone else’s game install.
heroes.commitHint: “Commit” only writes into the current Art Studio project finished assets. It does not hot-reload a running battle process. Use “Export pack” for the battle client. Style lock must be committed first. Batch action strips require a locked turnaround.
voice.title: Lines & voice
voice.lead: Defaults to Gemini-TTS. The game plays only six lines: select browse, intro, hurt (short), super, win, defeat. Normals and specials have no VO. Playback finishes the full line. “Generate & commit” writes into assets/game/.
voice.personaPlaceholder: e.g. young emperor, short lines, classical mixed with colloquial, drops low then bursts when angry.
voice.languageHint: Search by Chinese name, English name, or code. Google does not synthesize Khmer km-KH yet—use voice clone, or try th-TH / vi-VN.
voice.engineHint: Gemini voice uses the current Key. Cloud read / legacy clone need separate Cloud TTS access; Express does not support them.
viewport.cyanKeyTitle: Applies only when you click Commit / Overwrite commit. Flood-fills #00FFFF from image edges; gold/white particles remain. Drafts always keep the cyan backdrop for checking. “Re-key cyan” re-runs a stricter matte on already-committed game PNGs without re-splitting.
pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.hint: Drafts live in assets/studio/drafts/. “Commit” writes to this project’s assets/game/. For the battle client, “Export pack”, then --import or drop the zip into game/incoming/.
stages.exportAllTitle: Export every committed stage in this project
heroes.exportAllTitle: Export every committed hero in this project
portraits.listDeleteTitle: Delete the open portrait (drafts and exports)
portraits.listHint: Use “Del” on the right to remove a portrait. Pipeline: lock style → look/gear → write prompts → turnaround then other actions → split → de-cyan export.
status.default: Lock the game style first, then draw stages and heroes.
bodyScale.title: Body-scale workspace
bodyScale.guideLabelTitle: Library default 560px; scale 0.5×–1.5× (280–840px). Syncs game visualScale.
bodyScale.guideApplyTitle: Write for this hero and refresh guides
bodyScale.guideNote: Most heroes share the default height; change only for unusual silhouettes.
bodyScale.head: Head
bodyScale.playNote: Preview uses current per-frame slider ratios; does not write to the game.
bodyScale.bufferHint: Click a thumb to insert after the selection · frames still in buffer are discarded on save
bodyScale.pctTitle: Type a percent, 35–300 (must reach the top 1.5× guide)
bodyScale.feetLabelTitle: Positive lifts feet (character up), negative drops; guide stays on the idle baseline
bodyScale.feetPctTitle: Foot offset vs green line (commit px); + = lift, − = drop; range ±240
bodyScale.selectAllTitle: Select every frame in this sheet
bodyScale.moveLeftTitle: Move the selected contiguous block one step left
bodyScale.moveRightTitle: Move the selected contiguous block one step right
bodyScale.dupTitle: Duplicate selected frames after (reuse same sprites)
bodyScale.toBufferTitle: Move from timeline into remove buffer (discarded on save)
bodyScale.suggestTitle: Fill suggested percents from idle baseline (save still required to commit)
bodyScale.resplitTitle: Re-cut equal widths from the current committed strip
bodyScale.hint: Cyan/green guides are the shared reference torso height (default 560px; customize per hero above; 0.5×–1.5×). Preview snaps to both lines; jump apex may rise above cyan. Scale/feet/mirror write as-is; aerial sheets keep hang time. Timeline supports reuse, buffer, and horizontal mirror. The game uses the same visualScale formula—no special short/tall cases.
selectCrop.title: Crop select portrait
selectCrop.lead: The center box size is fixed. Drag the base image to move; scroll or slider to zoom. Commit is still 128×128.
selectCrop.hint: Box is locked—only move/zoom the image so faces stay similar on the card.
projectDlg.title: Switch project
projectDlg.aliasPlaceholder: e.g. HeroGame. Leave blank when creating to use the folder name
projectDlg.hint: Switch among listed projects. Pick an empty folder to create (alias helps distinguish; folder name is still the on-disk path). You cannot delete the current project—switch away first.
viewport.emptyPortraitBody: Click “New portrait” or open one from the list on the right.
viewport.emptyPortraitHtml: No portrait open Click “New portrait” or open one from the list on the right.
viewport.emptyHeroHtml: Viewport empty Write sheet prompts on the left and slots will appear here.
viewport.emptyPortraitFormHtml: Portrait / desk pet Fill look and accessories on the left, then write prompts—slots appear here.
